name: Supreme Industries Limited
industry: Plastic piping / packaging / consumer & industrial plastic products

moat_sources.name: efficient_scale
moat_sources.evidence_note: Largest Indian plastic-piping-and-products manufacturer by volume, 25+ plants nationally, capacity expansion to 1.5mn MT targeted by FY28 -- a real distribution/manufacturing-footprint scale lead over all but Astral/Finolex

moat_sources.name: pricing_power
moat_sources.evidence_note: PVC resin is a pass-through input but the pass-through is imperfect and lagged: recent quarter plastic-pipe realizations corrected ~4.1% YoY on resin-price swings, destocking and 'competitive pricing' language from company commentary; intense competition from both organized (Astral, Finolex, Prince, Ashirvad) and unorganized players caps durable pricing power -- this is a genuine weakness, not a strength, and should not be read as a moat

moat_sources.name: switching_costs
moat_sources.evidence_note: Multi-decade dealer/plumber distribution network typical of the organized pipe majors -- real but moderate, and shared with Astral/Finolex rather than unique to Supreme

moat_sources.name: cost_advantage
moat_sources.evidence_note: Scale-driven procurement and manufacturing efficiency support a >20% ROCE, but the underlying input (PVC/polypropylene) is a shared commodity so the cost edge over Astral/Finolex is one of degree, not kind

industry_context.phase_evidence: Organized Indian plastic-piping/products industry is now large and multi-player (Supreme, Astral, Finolex, Prince, Ashirvad and others) rather than an early formalization story; recent growth has decelerated (FY25->FY26 revenue +7.4%) and margins are pressured by PVC-price volatility and competitive/unorganized pricing -- consistent with a maturing, cyclical-industrial phase rather than a fresh inflection. The FY2025 anti-dumping duty on PVC imports is a real but incremental tailwind for organized domestic producers, not evidence of a structural re-rating inflection on its own.

bridge_assumptions.margin_delta_mechanism_note: Management guides FY27 EBITDA margin of 14-14.5% vs FY25's 13.7%, but this is a single forward-quarter guidance range set against a history of margin volatility driven by PVC resin swings -- not evidenced enough at Tier 3 to book as a durable margin-delta CAGR per the 6A discipline. Bridge is therefore run on volume/revenue growth only, with the exit multiple held flat rather than assuming re-rating.

variant_perception.market_belief: Priced by the market as India's largest, highest-quality, most diversified organized plastic-products compounder -- debt-free, scale-leading, and therefore deserving of a premium (~42-50x trailing) multiple.

notes: Tier 3/5 dossier built from WebSearch result snippets only -- screener.in, moneycontrol and other primary aggregators returned EGRESS_BLOCKED when fetched directly in this environment, so nothing here rises above Tier 3 (search-surfaced secondary/aggregator commentary), and the full 2021-2026 balance-sheet series is a Tier 5 backcast anchored only on FY25/FY26 revenue and PAT. Per M6, none of these figures should be allowed to single-handedly clear a NAVY gate; treat this as a screening-stage read, not investment-grade research. Key honest judgment calls: pricing_power moat rated RED/ERODING (real evidence of resin-driven realization correction and competitive-pricing pressure, not a strength); industry phase called MATURE rather than INFLECTION given multi-player competitive intensity and decelerating growth; variant_perception left answered=False because no credible mispricing case (bull or bear) could be substantiated from available data -- the stock's premium multiple looks like the market already pricing in its quality/scale leadership; m5_protocol_complete=False because this was a single research pass, not the full adversarial protocol.
